note.backdrop: Friday closed at its lows: the S&P 500 fund -3.64%, the Nasdaq 100 fund -5.67%, the Dow fund -1.98%, the Russell 2000 fund -2.88% (StockTitan). It was the S&P 500's seventh loss in a row. The S&P 500 and Dow funds ended in a correction, about 11.5% and 11.4% below their records, and the Dow fund's week (-8.0%) was its worst since March 2020 (StockTitan). In the bank's quotes the VIX closed at 35.89 (+26.2%) and the 10-year yield at 4.91%, about 0.14 points lower on the day; gold settled at $3,539 (-3.98%) and bitcoin was -10.1% on Yahoo's day. A Federal Reserve governor said that 'waiting longer to implement rate increases risks getting behind the curve' (Fed, via StockTitan): the selloff came with no promise of easier money. Anthropic closed at $88.91, -8.5%, above its $83 offer price. After hours the S&P 500 fund is +1.1% and the Nasdaq 100 fund +1.5% (the check); Nvidia was +3.27% at 6:02 p.m. ET (StockTitan). The check's after-close driver lines are measured from Thursday's bars again (futures -3.2%, gold -4.0%, bitcoin -10.0% are Friday's whole moves): the stocks most tied to gold and bitcoin rose after hours (Newmont +1.6%, Strategy +2.2%) while those lines imply -2.7% and -12.9%. So the market-wide flag is false.
